subject: ThirdWave SDK gateway change request & compatibility checklist
messages:
From: Sophia Chen <sophia.chen@thirdwave.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Nate Ortiz <nate@thirdwave.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SDK gateway change — impact to ThirdWave connector

Hi Grace,

Quick note from ThirdWave engineering: our platform team is planning to migrate the gateway layer that your SDK integrates with from the legacy /v1/pipe endpoints to the new aggregated /api/streams endpoint. The migration is scheduled for May 15.

We rely on Redwood's client SDK for automatic retry semantics and prefix-key caching. The new gateway changes a couple of headers and merges streaming semantics; we believe the behavior will be functionally compatible but need to confirm the SDK will continue to handle KV caching and the connection upgrade flow.

Can we ask for: 
- Confirmation whether Redwood's JS and Python SDKs will support the new /api/streams without a breaking major bump?
- A short compatibility matrix indicating which behavior change (if any) will affect our connector (auth header change, stream framing, retry backoff).
- If a shim is required on our side, whether Redwood would consider providing a minimal shim design or patch to the SDK to preserve the current integration until we can fully migrate.

We're happy to jump on a short sync. Proposed times: Thu 4/13 10:00–11:00 PDT or Fri 4/14 08:30–09:00 PDT.

Attaching a CSV with the surface area we tested.

Thanks,
Sophia
Director of Integrations
ThirdWave

Attachments: thirdwave-compat-matrix-v1.csv

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Chen <sophia.chen@thirdwave.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK gateway change — impact to ThirdWave connector

Hi Sophia — thanks for the heads up and the attachment, that matrix is helpful.

Short answers up front:
- We do not intend to ship a breaking major bump for the client experience. The runtime team has designed the /api/streams endpoint to be backwards-compatible for common SDK flows (streaming + prefix KV cache).
- That said, there are two behavioral deltas you should watch: an auth header canonicalization (we now prefer X-RW-Auth over Authorization for load-balancer metrics) and an additional keepalive ping that can affect long-lived streaming connections absent client-side handling.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal triage with runtime/SDK owners to validate retry/backoff and connection upgrade handling. Marcus will lead.
2) Provide a short "compatibility shim" proposal your engineering team can drop in if you want to move before we ship the client patch. Vanessa will draft the shim design and a small reference implementation.
3) Schedule a 30-minute technical sync to walk through the matrix and the shim. I'm available Thu 4/13 10:00 PDT.

Marissa — can you add this to the partner backlog and open a GitHub draft PR for the shim? Marcus — can you confirm whether the keepalive ping will require SDK-level changes or a patch in the runtime (server-side)?

Sophia — we'll attach the proposed shim design and a quick test plan in the follow-up.

Best,
Grace
Head of Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK gateway change — impact to ThirdWave connector

Grace — quick triage notes from runtime:
- Keepalive ping: Server will send a 10s lightweight ping on streams longer than 60s. Most SDKs that rely on underlying HTTP/2/TCP connection should be fine, but a thin shim that acknowledges pings (or converts them to no-op) is trivial.
- Auth header canonicalization: We'll accept both Authorization and X-RW-Auth for a one-quarter transition window. We'll log deprecation warnings at the LB level if Authorization is used.
- Retry/backoff: No change to semantics; current client exponential backed jitter still works.

I started a draft PR with a proposed shim implementation for the JS SDK (source branch: partners/thirdwave-shim). The design is intentionally minimal: intercept the fetch/websocket factory, map Authorization to X-RW-Auth if needed, and swallow keepalive pings for streams older than 60s.

Attaching a short design doc: proposed-shim-design.pdf. We'll also add an integration test that replays ThirdWave's CSV scenarios.

Action items: Marcus -> finalize PR and tests; Vanessa -> review the shim for compatibility with epoched API keys; Marissa -> create partner ticket and add to the shared roadmap.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Chen <sophia.chen@thirdwave.ai>, Nate Ortiz <nate@thirdwave.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SDK gateway change — impact to ThirdWave connector

Hi Sophia / Nate — thanks for the sync today. Recap and plan below so everyone has the same view.

Recap:
- Redwood will support both Authorization and X-RW-Auth for the next quarter; no immediate breaking change.
- Runtime will not break streaming semantics; keepalive pings will be present but the JS/Python shims will silently handle them.
- Draft shim PR created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/thirdwave-shims/pull/82) and includes unit/integration tests that cover the rows in your matrix.

Plan (owner / target dates):
- Marcus: finalize PR and land tests — target 2028-04-28.
- Vanessa: validate shim with epoched key workflow — target 2028-04-26.
- Marissa: publish partner-facing compatibility note and link to PR — target 2028-04-27.
- ThirdWave (Sophia/Nate): run the supplied test matrix against the shim branch and confirm no regressions — target 2028-05-05.

If everything passes, Redwood will schedule the gateway cut for 2028-05-15 with a formal deprecation email and a documented 90-day transition period. If you need an accelerated fallback plan we can arrange a temporary traffic rule for your tenant ID.

Closing notes: attaching the two artifacts we discussed. Please reply with any changes to the timeline.

Best,
Grace
Head of Partner Integrations

Attachments: proposed-shim-design.pdf, thirdwave-compat-matrix-v1.csv
